react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge on two biological axes despite the apparent chemical heterogeneity of the input set. RaMP multi-database ORA identified the broad 'Metabolism' super-pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1430728, FDR=6.9×10⁻⁵) and, more specifically, amino-acid metabolism in triple-negative breast cancer cells (WP:WP5213, FDR=6.9×10⁻⁵) as the top-ranked hits, both driven by glutathione and phosphoserine co-enrichment. Trans-sulfuration and one-carbon metabolism (WP:WP2525, FDR=3.6×10⁻⁴) further implicates the glutathione–cysteine axis, consistent with its role in redox buffering. Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=3.6×10⁻⁴) captures the coumarin–glutathione pair, reflecting Phase I/II xenobiotic metabolism. Mummichog confirmed Glycine/serine/alanine and threonine metabolism (p=0.0088) and Glutathione Metabolism (p=0.0497), extending the signal to the m/z network level. MetaboAnalystR independently ranked Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) metabolism (hsa00770, p=0.0494) as the single strongest KEGG hit, consistent with the CoA biosynthesis hit from Mummichog (rank 7), indicating that the treatment perturbs both the glutathione redox system and pantothenate–CoA homeostasis. Five metabolites (glutathione, phosphoserine, coumarin, pantothenic acid, benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide I) resolved to clean ChEBI canonical forms with no InChIKey conflicts, confirming that the cross-tool convergence reflects true biological signal rather than namespace artefacts.

  "narrative_text": "Three complementary enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-network activity, and Reactome ORA) converge on two biological axes. The first is xenobiotic metabolism and oxidative stress, where glutathione (C00051) and coumarin (C05851) are the shared driver metabolites detected by both RaMP (Biological Oxidations, REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=3.6×10⁻³) and Mummichog (Xenobiotics Metabolism, MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism, p=7.3×10⁻³). The second axis is one-carbon/two-sulfur metabolism, where glutathione and O-phospho-L-serine (C01005) co-enrich in Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways (WP:WP2525, FDR=3.6×10⁻⁴, RaMP rank 3) and in the top Mummichog hit Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism, p=7.3×10⁻³). Pantothenic acid (C00864) independently reaches significance in Vitamin B5 - CoA biosynthesis from pantothenate (MUMM:vitamin_b5_coa_biosynthesis_from_pantothenate, p=4.6×10⁻²). Glutathione participates in two distinct reactions within these pathways: as a substrate of the glutathione S-transferase S-conjugation reaction (R01696) in xenobiotic metabolism, and as a substrate of cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS, R01476) in the trans-sulfuration pathway. Coumarin appears as a co-enriched member in both xenobiotic metabolism and the coumarin-specific tyrosine metabolism branch. Phosphoserine is confirmed as a member of the glycine/serine/alanine/threonine metabolism network. Cross-paradigm convergence on glutathione and coumarin across xenobiotics and oxidative-stress pathways indicates that the treatment perturbs both Phase-I/II xenobiotic clearance and the cellular redox-buffering system, with pantothenate-CoA homeostasis co-affected as a cofactor-biosynthesis readout.",

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-network activity, and Reactome ORA) converge on two biological axes. The first is xenobiotic metabolism and oxidative stress, where glutathione (C00051) and coumarin (C05851) are the shared driver metabolites detected by both RaMP (Biological Oxidations, REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=3.6×10⁻³) and Mummichog (Xenobiotics Metabolism, MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism, p=7.3×10⁻³). The second axis is one-carbon/two-sulfur metabolism, where glutathione and O-phospho-L-serine (C01005) co-enrich in Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways (WP:WP2525, FDR=3.6×10⁻⁴, RaMP rank 3) and in the top Mummichog hit Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism, p=7.3×10⁻³). Pantothenic acid (C00864) independently reaches significance in Vitamin B5 - CoA biosynthesis from pantothenate (MUMM:vitamin_b5_coa_biosynthesis_from_pantothenate, p=4.6×10⁻²). Glutathione participates in two distinct reactions within these pathways: as a substrate of the glutathione S-transferase S-conjugation reaction (R01696) in xenobiotic metabolism, and as a substrate of cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS, R01476) in the trans-sulfuration pathway. Coumarin appears as a co-enriched member in both xenobiotic metabolism and the coumarin-specific tyrosine metabolism branch. Phosphoserine is confirmed as a member of the glycine/serine/alanine/threonine metabolism network. Cross-paradigm convergence on glutathione and coumarin across xenobiotics and oxidative-stress pathways indicates that the treatment perturbs both Phase-I/II xenobiotic clearance and the cellular redox-buffering system, with pantothenate-CoA homeostasis co-affected as a cofactor-biosynthesis readout.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge on two biological axes despite the apparent chemical heterogeneity of the input set. RaMP multi-database ORA identified the broad 'Metabolism' super-pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1430728, FDR=6.9×10⁻⁵) and, more specifically, amino-acid metabolism in triple-negative breast cancer cells (WP:WP5213, FDR=6.9×10⁻⁵) as the top-ranked hits, both driven by glutathione and phosphoserine co-enrichment. Trans-sulfuration and one-carbon metabolism (WP:WP2525, FDR=3.6×10⁻⁴) further implicates the glutathione–cysteine axis, consistent with its role in redox buffering. Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=3.6×10⁻⁴) captures the coumarin–glutathione pair, reflecting Phase I/II xenobiotic metabolism. Mummichog confirmed Glycine/serine/alanine and threonine metabolism (p=0.0088) and Glutathione Metabolism (p=0.0497), extending the signal to the m/z network level. MetaboAnalystR independently ranked Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) metabolism (hsa00770, p=0.0494) as the single strongest KEGG hit, consistent with the CoA biosynthesis hit from Mummichog (rank 7), indicating that the treatment perturbs both the glutathione redox system and pantothenate–CoA homeostasis. Five metabolites (glutathione, phosphoserine, coumarin, pantothenic acid, benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide I) resolved to clean ChEBI canonical forms with no InChIKey conflicts, confirming that the cross-tool convergence reflects true biological signal rather than namespace artefacts.
